segments.title: Opening News Desk & Kendall Visit
segments.notes: Case opens the broadcast post-award-show, fields chat, reveals Kendall napping in the 'noups room,' and demos a Vo weak automatic scrubber brush before pivoting to news.

segments.title: Epstein Documents with Ramon Salazar
segments.notes: Case summons Resident Evil's Ramon Salazar to co-anchor the unsealed Epstein court documents; Salazar reads the Independent coverage, names Trump, Clinton, Prince Andrew, Dershowitz, Lucas, Spacey, Jackson, and Hawking, then exits via trap door.

segments.title: Pepito Wrap & Handoff to Streets
segments.notes: Pepito delivers a freestyle wrap at chat's request, then accepts a rap battle challenge against Trip Bradstein on location.

segments.title: Trip Hop: Pepito vs. Trip Bradstein Rap Battle
segments.notes: Trip Bradstein finds a 'dog freestyle beat' and trades verses with Pepito; chat supplies questions; Pepito claims orphan status and best-mom loyalty to Fiona; Trip dubs the genre 'trip hop.'

segments.title: Belly Button Debate: Dogs & Cats
segments.notes: Munch and Crum debate whether dogs and cats have belly buttons; Munch argues mammals need umbilical cords, Crum invents a 'slop shoot' egg-birth theory; chat poll gives Munch a narrow win; Crum storms off to 'take a huge screaming shit of success.'

segments.title: Case Blackwell Therapy Session
segments.notes: Case visits Dr. Chath; topics include Peter Gibbon sightings, Epstein list exclusion anxiety, collaboration fears, ass-eating flexibility hypotheticals, and Liliana's absence; Dr. Chath ends with a pre-recorded sign-off.

segments.title: At the Movies: Trailers with Trent & Chris
segments.notes: Parole officer Chris and movie correspondent Trent react to Saltburn, Marvel's Echo, and the public-domain horror Mickey Mouse Trap; Chris relates to Saltburn's rich-party anxiety, defends Kingpin's muscle mass, and apologizes for disrespecting low-budget directors.

segments.title: Streets Wrap-Up & Raid
segments.notes: Pepito and Trip return for a second rap round on a 'hard dark type beat'; Pepito declares himself a 'fuck master' (redefined as sweet devotion to Fiona); Case raids Ricky Peacock with a 'Viva Pepito' message.

characters.name: Pepito
characters.notes: executive producer. Delivered a wrap, rap-battled Trip Bradstein twice on location, claimed orphan origin, and received a new emote.

characters.name: Crum (Leonard Crum)
characters.notes: debate analyst. Argued dogs and cats hatch from eggs via a 'slop shoot,' lost the belly-button poll by three votes, and fled to the bathroom claiming victory-induced bowel emergency.

characters.name: Munch (Ralph Munchcut)
characters.notes: debate analyst. Defended mammalian umbilical cords, won the belly-button poll by a razor-thin margin, and mocked Crum's post-loss spiral.

characters.name: Kendelle
characters.notes: in-studio contributor. Briefly appeared napping in the 'noups room,' declined to stream, and left to clean the bathtub with the new scrubber brush.

characters.name: Ramon Salazar
characters.notes: guest correspondent. Resident Evil castellan co-anchored the Epstein document dump, recited associate names, and exited through a trap door.

characters.name: Trip Bradstein
characters.notes: field correspondent. Hosted two street rap sessions with Pepito, coined 'trip hop,' and produced beats from the park.

characters.name: Dr. Chath
characters.notes: therapist. Conducted a chaotic session with Case, fielded chat questions, and ended with a pre-recorded 'bless up Kyle' sign-off.

characters.name: Peter Gibbon
characters.notes: news stowaway. Reported live from a Trump rally at the Dunskan Donuts Financial Arena after overstaying the award-show rental.

characters.name: Chris
characters.notes: parole officer. Supervised Trent at the movie theater, disclosed credit-card debt and ADHD, and bonded over Kingpin's musculature.

characters.name: Trent
characters.notes: movie correspondent. Presented trailers for Saltburn, Echo, and Mickey Mouse Trap from the theater.

storylines.beat: Crum's gambling-addiction arc not directly advanced, but his 'slop shoot' biology invention and narrow poll loss reinforce his pattern of humiliating defeats.

lore_notes.fact: Has a dedicated 'noups room' (news + naps) in the studio where she sleeps during broadcasts. [14:48]
Claims to have been born from an egg via 'sloop shoot' and identifies as an orphan; declares Fiona his 'best mommy' despite Trip's skepticism. [54:42]
Coined the genre 'trip hop' for his street rap segments. [1:45:47]
Plans to move to a new house with a separate office around February 2024, enabling longer streams without disturbing Kendall. [20:48]
Murder mystery stream (with Fianna and Kevin) remains planned over a year later; Case cites time, money, scheduling, and 'lube' as hurdles. [24:29]
New Pepito emote saved and ready for upload. [1:21:04]

episode_summary: Case Blackwell returns from the award show to a chaotic news night: Kendall demos a scrubber brush in the 'noups room,' Ramon Salazar materializes to read the unsealed Epstein documents, and Pepito engages in two rap battles with Trip Bradstein on the streets. Munch edges Crum in a belly-button poll, prompting Crum's theatrical victory shit, while Case's therapy session veers into ass-eating hypotheticals. The broadcast closes with trailer reactions at the movies and a raid on Ricky Peacock.
